translation.text: Slaying these sons of Dhritarâshtra, what pleasure can be ours, O Janârdana? Killing these desperadoes, sin will but take hold of us.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Therefore we should not kill the sons of Dhritarâshtra, our relatives; for how, killing our kinsmen, may we be happy, O Mâdhava?

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Although these, with intelligence overpowered by greed, see no guilt in the destruction of a family, no crime in hostility to friends,

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Why should not we learn to turn away from such a sin, O Janârdana, who see the evils in the destruction of a family?

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: In the destruction of a family the immemorial family traditions perish; in the perishing of tradition, lawlessness overcomes the whole family;

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Owing to predominance of lawlessness, O Krishna, the women of the family become corrupt; women corrupted, O Vârshneya, there ariseth caste confusion;

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: This confusion draggeth to hell the slayers of the family, and the family; for their ancestors fall, deprived of rice-balls and libations.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: By these caste-confusing misdeeds of the slayers of the family, the everlasting caste customs and family customs are abolished.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: The abode of the men whose family customs are extinguished, O Janârdana, is everlastingly in hell. Thus have we heard.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Alas! in committing a great sin are we engaged, we who are endeavouring to kill our kindred from greed of the pleasures of kingship.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: If the sons of Dhritarâshtra, weapon in hand, should slay me, unresisting, unarmed, in the battle, that would for me be the better.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Sanjaya said: Having thus spoken on the battle-field, Arjuna sank down on the seat of the chariot, casting away his bow and arrow, his mind overborne by grief.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Sanjaya said: To him thus with pity overcome, with smarting brimming eyes, despondent, Madhusûdana spake these words:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: The Blessed Lord said: Whence hath this dejection befallen thee in this perilous strait, ignoble, heaven-closing, infamous, O Arjuna?

original.text:
श्री भगवानुवाच
कुतस्त्वा कश्मलमिदं विषमे समुपस्थितम्।

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Yield not to impotence, O Partha! it doth not befit thee. Shake off this paltry faint-heartedness! Stand up, Parantapa!

original.text:

क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परन्तप

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Arjuna said: How, O Madhusûdana, shall I attack Bhîshma and Drona with arrows in battle, they who are worthy of reverence, O slayer of foes?

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Better in this world to eat even the beggar's crust than to slay these most noble Gurus. Slaying these Gurus, our well-wishers, I should taste of blood-besprinkled feasts.

original.text:

हत्वार्थकामांस्तु गुरूनिहैव
भुञ्जीय भोगान् रुधिरप्रदिग्धान्

transliteration.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Nor know I which for us be the better, that we conquer them or they conquer us—these, whom having slain we should not care to live, even these arrayed against us, the sons of Dhritarâshtra.

यानेव हत्वा न जिजीविषाम
स्तेऽवस्थिताः प्रमुखे धार्तराष्ट्राः

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: My heart is weighed down with the vice of faintness; my mind is confused as to duty. I ask thee which may be the better—that tell me decisively. I am thy disciple, suppliant to Thee; teach me.

original.text:

यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्िचतं ब्रूहि तन्मे

śiṣyaste'haṃ śādhi māṃ tvāṃ prapannam
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: For I see not that it would drive away this anguish that withers up my senses, if I should attain unrivalled monarchy on earth, or even the sovereignty of the Shining Ones.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Sanjaya said: Gudâkesha, conqueror of his foes, having thus addressed Hrishîkesha and said to Govinda, "I will not fight!", became silent.

original.text:

एवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशं गुडाकेशः परन्तप।
न योत्स्य इति गोविन्दमुक्त्वा तूष्णीं बभूव ह

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Then Hrishîkesha, smiling, as it were, O Bhârata, spake these words to him, despondent, in the midst of the two armies:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: The Blessed Lord said: Thou grievest for those that should not be griev ed for, yet speakest words of wisdom. The wise grieve neither for the living nor for the dead.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Nor at any time verily was I not, nor thou, nor these princes of men, nor verily shall we ever cease to be, hereafter.

original.text:

न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम्

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: As the dweller in the body experienceth in the body childhood, youth, old age, so passeth he on to another body; the steadfast one grieveth not thereat.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: The contacts of matter, O son of Kuntî, giving cold and heat, pleasure and pain, they come and go, impermanent; endure them bravely, O Bhârata.

original.text:

आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत

mātrāsparśāstu kaunteya śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhadāḥ|

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: The man whom these torment not, O chief of men, balanced in pain and pleasure, steadfast, he is fitted for immortality.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: The unreal hath no being; the real never ceaseth to be; the truth about both hath been perceived by the seers of the essence of things.

original.text:

उभयोरपि दृष्टोऽन्तस्त्वनयोस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Know That to be indestructible by whom all this is pervaded. Nor can any work the destruction of that imperishable One.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: These bodies of the embodied One, who is eternal, indestructible and immeasurable, are known as finite. Therefore fight, O Bhârata.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: He who regardeth this as a slayer, and he who thinketh he is slain, both of them are ignorant. He slayeth not, nor is he slain.

original.text:
य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम्।
उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: He is not born, nor doth he die; nor having been, ceaseth he any more to be; unborn, perpetual, eternal and ancient, he is not slain when the body is slaughtered.

original.text:

न्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः।
अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Who knoweth him indestructible, perpetual, unborn, undiminishing, how can that man slay, O Pârtha, or cause to be slain?

original.text:

कथं स पुरुषः पार्थ कं घातयति हन्ति कम्

kathaṃ sa puruṣaḥ pārtha kaṃ ghātayati hanti kam
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: As a man, casting off worn-out garments, taketh new ones, so the dweller in the body, casting off worn-out bodies, entereth into others that are new.

original.text:
वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहाय
नवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि।
तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णा
न्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही

transliteration.text:
vāsāṃsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya
navāni gṛhṇāti naro'parāṇi|
tathā śarīrāṇi vihāya jīrṇā
nyanyāni saṃyāti navāni dehī
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Weapons cleave him not, nor fire burneth him, nor waters wet him, nor wind drieth him away.

original.text:
नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः।
न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः

transliteration.text:
nainaṃ chindanti śastrāṇi nainaṃ dahati pāvakaḥ|
na cainaṃ kledayantyāpo na śoṣayati mārutaḥ
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Uncleavable he, incombustible he, and indeed neither to be wetted nor dried away; perpetual, all-pervasive, stable, immovable, ancient.

original.text:
अच्छेद्योऽयमदाह्योऽयमक्लेद्योऽशोष्य एव च।
नित्यः सर्वगतः स्थाणुरचलोऽयं सनातनः

transliteration.text:
acchedyo'yamadāhyo'yamakledyo'śoṣya eva ca|
nityaḥ sarvagataḥ sthāṇuracalo'yaṃ sanātanaḥ
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Unmanifest, unthinkable, immutable, he is called; therefore knowing him as such, thou shouldst not grieve.

original.text:
अव्यक्तोऽयमचिन्त्योऽयमविकार्योऽयमुच्यते।
तस्मादेवं विदित्वैनं नानुशोचितुमर्हसि

transliteration.text:
avyakto'yamacintyo'yamavikāryo'yamucyate|
tasmādevaṃ viditvainaṃ nānuśocitumarhasi
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Or if thou thinkest of him as being constantly born and constantly dying, even then, O mighty-armed, thou shouldst not grieve.

original.text:
अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम्।
तथापि त्वं महाबाहो नैवं शोचितुमर्हसि

transliteration.text:
atha cainaṃ nityajātaṃ nityaṃ vā manyase mṛtam|
tathāpi tvaṃ mahābāho naivaṃ śocitumarhasi
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: For certain is death for the born, and certain is birth for the dead; therefore over the inevitable thou shouldst not grieve.

original.text:
जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च।
तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि

transliteration.text:
jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyurdhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca|
tasmādaparihārye'rthe na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Beings are unmanifest in their origin, manifest in their midmost state, O Bhârata, unmanifest likewise are they in dissolution. What room then for lamentation?

original.text:
अव्यक्तादीनि भूतानि व्यक्तमध्यानि भारत।
अव्यक्तनिधनान्येव तत्र का परिदेवना

transliteration.text:
avyaktādīni bhūtāni vyaktamadhyāni bhārata|
avyaktanidhanānyeva tatra kā paridevanā
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: As marvellous one regardeth him; as marvellous another speaketh thereof; as marvellous another heareth thereof; yet having heard none indeed understandeth.

original.text:
आश्चर्यवत्पश्यति कश्चिदेन
माश्चर्यवद्वदति तथैव चान्यः।
आश्चर्यवच्चैनमन्यः श्रृणोति
श्रुत्वाप्येनं वेद न चैव कश्चित्

transliteration.text:
āścaryavatpaśyati kaścidena
māścaryavadvadati tathaiva cānyaḥ|
āścaryavaccainamanyaḥ śrṛṇoti
śrutvāpyenaṃ veda na caiva kaścit
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: This dweller in the body of everyone is ever invulnerable, O Bhârata; therefore thou shouldst not grieve for any creature.

original.text:
देही नित्यमवध्योऽयं देहे सर्वस्य भारत।
तस्मात्सर्वाणि भूतानि न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि

transliteration.text:
dehī nityamavadhyo'yaṃ dehe sarvasya bhārata|
tasmātsarvāṇi bhūtāni na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Further, looking to thine own duty thou shouldst not tremble; for there is nothing more welcome to a Kshattriya than righteous war.

original.text:
स्वधर्ममपि चावेक्ष्य न विकम्पितुमर्हसि।
धर्म्याद्धि युद्धाछ्रेयोऽन्यत्क्षत्रियस्य न विद्यते

transliteration.text:
svadharmamapi cāvekṣya na vikampitumarhasi|
dharmyāddhi yuddhāchreyo'nyatkṣatriyasya na vidyate
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Happy the Kshattriyas, O Pârtha, who obtain such a fight, offered unsought as an open door to heaven.

original.text:
यदृच्छया चोपपन्नं स्वर्गद्वारमपावृतम्।
सुखिनः क्षत्रियाः पार्थ लभन्ते युद्धमीदृशम्

transliteration.text:
yadṛcchayā copapannaṃ svargadvāramapāvṛtam|
sukhinaḥ kṣatriyāḥ pārtha labhante yuddhamīdṛśam
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: But if thou wilt not carry on this righteous warfare, then casting away thine own duty and thine honour, thou wilt incur sin.

original.text:
अथ चैत्त्वमिमं धर्म्यं संग्रामं न करिष्यसि।
ततः स्वधर्मं कीर्तिं च हित्वा पापमवाप्स्यसि

transliteration.text:
atha caittvamimaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ na kariṣyasi|
tataḥ svadharmaṃ kīrtiṃ ca hitvā pāpamavāpsyasi
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Men will recount thy perpetual dishonour, and, to one highly esteemed, dishonour exceedeth death.

original.text:
अकीर्तिं चापि भूतानि कथयिष्यन्ति तेऽव्ययाम्।
संभावितस्य चाकीर्तिर्मरणादतिरिच्यते

transliteration.text:
akīrtiṃ cāpi bhūtāni kathayiṣyanti te'vyayām|
saṃbhāvitasya cākīrtirmaraṇādatiricyate
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: The great car-warriors will think thee fled from the battle from fear, and thou, that wast highly thought of by them, wilt be lightly held.

original.text:
भयाद्रणादुपरतं मंस्यन्ते त्वां महारथाः।
येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम्

transliteration.text:
bhayādraṇāduparataṃ maṃsyante tvāṃ mahārathāḥ|
yeṣāṃ ca tvaṃ bahumato bhūtvā yāsyasi lāghavam
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Many unseemly words will be spoken by thine enemies, slandering thy strength; what more painful than that?

original.text:
अवाच्यवादांश्च बहून् वदिष्यन्ति तवाहिताः।
निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम्

transliteration.text:
avācyavādāṃśca bahūn vadiṣyanti tavāhitāḥ|
nindantastava sāmarthyaṃ tato duḥkhataraṃ nu kim
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Slain, thou wilt obtain heaven; victorious, thou wilt enjoy the earth; therefore stand up, O son of Kuntî, resolute to fight.

original.text:
हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम्।
तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ कौन्तेय युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयः

transliteration.text:
hato vā prāpsyasi svargaṃ jitvā vā bhokṣyase mahīm|
tasmāduttiṣṭha kaunteya yuddhāya kṛtaniścayaḥ
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Taking as equal pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat, gird thee for the battle; thus thou shalt not incur sin.

original.text:
सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ।
ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि

transliteration.text:
sukhaduḥkhe same kṛtvā lābhālābhau jayājayau|
tato yuddhāya yujyasva naivaṃ pāpamavāpsyasi
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: This teaching set forth to thee is in accordance with the Sâñkhya; hear it now according to the Yoga, imbued with which teaching, O Pârtha, thou shalt cast away the bonds of action.

original.text:
एषा तेऽभिहिता सांख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां श्रृणु।
बुद्ध्यायुक्तो यया पार्थ कर्मबन्धं प्रहास्यसि

transliteration.text:
eṣā te'bhihitā sāṃkhye buddhiryoge tvimāṃ śrṛṇu|
buddhyāyukto yayā pārtha karmabandhaṃ prahāsyasi
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: In this there is no loss of effort, nor is there transgression. Even a little of this knowledge protects from great fear.

original.text:
नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते।
स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात्

transliteration.text:
nehābhikramanāśo'sti pratyavāyo na vidyate|
svalpamapyasya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: The determinate Reason is but one-pointed, O joy of the Kurus; many-branched and endless are the thoughts of the irresolute.

original.text:
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन।
बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम्

transliteration.text:
vyavasāyātmikā buddhirekeha kurunandana|
bahuśākhā hyanantāśca buddhayo'vyavasāyinām
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Flowery speech is uttered by the foolish, rejoicing in the letter of the Vedas, O Pârtha, saying: "There is naught but this";

original.text:
यामिमां पुष्पितां वाचं प्रवदन्त्यविपश्चितः।
वेदवादरताः पार्थ नान्यदस्तीति वादिनः

transliteration.text:
yāmimāṃ puṣpitāṃ vācaṃ pravadantyavipaścitaḥ|
vedavādaratāḥ pārtha nānyadastīti vādinaḥ
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: With desire for self, with heaven for goal, they offer birth as the fruit of action, and prescribe many and various ceremonies for the attainment of pleasure and lordship.

original.text:
कामात्मानः स्वर्गपरा जन्मकर्मफलप्रदाम्।
क्रियाविशेषबहुलां भोगैश्वर्यगतिं प्रति

transliteration.text:
kāmātmānaḥ svargaparā janmakarmaphalapradām|
kriyāviśeṣabahulāṃ bhogaiśvaryagatiṃ prati
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: For them who cling to pleasure and lordship, whose minds are captivated by such teaching, is not designed this determinate Reason, on contemplation steadily bent.

original.text:
भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयापहृतचेतसाम्।
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते

transliteration.text:
bhogaiśvaryaprasaktānāṃ tayāpahṛtacetasām|
vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ samādhau na vidhīyate
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: The Vedas deal with the three attributes; be thou above these three attributes, O Arjuna; beyond the pairs of opposites, ever steadfast in purity, careless of possessions, full of the Self.

original.text:
त्रैगुण्यविषया वेदा निस्त्रैगुण्यो भवार्जुन।
निर्द्वन्द्वो नित्यसत्त्वस्थो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान्

transliteration.text:
traiguṇyaviṣayā vedā nistraiguṇyo bhavārjuna|
nirdvandvo nityasattvastho niryogakṣema ātmavān
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: All the Vedas are as useful to an enlightened Brâhmana as is a tank in a place covered all over with water.

original.text:
यावानर्थ उदपाने सर्वतः संप्लुतोदके।
तावान्सर्वेषु वेदेषु ब्राह्मणस्य विजानतः

transliteration.text:
yāvānartha udapāne sarvataḥ saṃplutodake|
tāvānsarveṣu vedeṣu brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Thy business is with the action only, never with its fruits; so let not the fruit of action be thy motive, nor be thou to inaction attached.

original.text:
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन।
मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि

transliteration.text:
karmaṇyevādhikāraste mā phaleṣu kadācana|
mā karmaphalaheturbhūrmā te saṅgo'stvakarmaṇi
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Perform action, O Dhananjaya, dwelling in union with the divine, renouncing attachments and balanced evenly in success and failure: equilibrium is called yoga.

original.text:
योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय।
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते

transliteration.text:
yogasthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā dhanañjaya|
siddhyasiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṃ yoga ucyate
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Far lower than the Yoga of Discrimination is action, O Dhananjaya. Take thou refuge in the Pure Reason; pitiable are they who work for fruit.

original.text:
दूरेण ह्यवरं कर्म बुद्धियोगाद्धनञ्जय।
बुद्धौ शरणमन्विच्छ कृपणाः फलहेतवः

transliteration.text:
dūreṇa hyavaraṃ karma buddhiyogāddhanañjaya|
buddhau śaraṇamanviccha kṛpaṇāḥ phalahetavaḥ
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: United to the Pure Reason one abandoneth here both good and evil deeds; therefore cleave thou to yoga; yoga is skill in action.

original.text:
बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते।
तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम्

transliteration.text:
buddhiyukto jahātīha ubhe sukṛtaduṣkṛte|
tasmādyogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: The Sages, united to the Pure Reason, renounce the fruit which action yieldeth, and, liberated from the bonds of birth, they go to the blissful seat.

original.text:
कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः।
जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ताः पदं गच्छन्त्यनामयम्

transliteration.text:
karmajaṃ buddhiyuktā hi phalaṃ tyaktvā manīṣiṇaḥ|
janmabandhavinirmuktāḥ padaṃ gacchantyanāmayam
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: When thy mind shall escape from this tangle of delusion, then thou shalt rise to indifference as to what has been heard and shall be heard.

original.text:
यदा ते मोहकलिलं बुद्धिर्व्यतितरिष्यति।
तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च

transliteration.text:
yadā te mohakalilaṃ buddhirvyatitariṣyati|
tadā gantāsi nirvedaṃ śrotavyasya śrutasya ca
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: When thy mind, bewildered by the Scriptures, shall stand immovable, fixed in contemplation, then shalt thou attain unto yoga.

original.text:
श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला।
समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि

transliteration.text:
śrutivipratipannā te yadā sthāsyati niścalā|
samādhāvacalā buddhistadā yogamavāpsyasi
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Arjuna said: What the mark, of him who is stable of mind, steadfast in contemplation, O Keshava? How doth the stable-minded talk, how doth he sit, how walk?

original.text:
अर्जुन उवाच
स्थितप्रज्ञस्य का भाषा समाधिस्थस्य केशव।
स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम्

transliteration.text:
arjuna uvāca
sthitaprajñasya kā bhāṣā samādhisthasya keśava|
sthitadhīḥ kiṃ prabhāṣeta kimāsīta vrajeta kim
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: The Blessed Lord said: When a man abandoneth, O Pârtha, all the desires of the heart, and is satisfied in the Self by the Self, then is he called stable in mind.

original.text:
श्री भगवानुवाच
प्रजहाति यदा कामान् सर्वान् पार्थ मनोगतान्।
आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः स्थितप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते

transliteration.text:
śrī bhagavānuvāca
prajahāti yadā kāmān sarvān pārtha manogatān|
ātmanyevātmanā tuṣṭaḥ sthitaprajñastadocyate
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: He whose mind is free from anxiety amid pains, indifferent amid pleasures, loosed from passion, fear and anger, is called a sage of stable mind.

original.text:
दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः।
वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते

transliteration.text:
duḥkheṣvanudvignamanāḥ sukheṣu vigataspṛhaḥ|
vītarāgabhayakrodhaḥ sthitadhīrmunirucyate
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: He who on every side is without attachments, whatever hap of fair and foul, who neither likes nor dislikes, of such a one the understanding is well poised.

original.text:
यः सर्वत्रानभिस्नेहस्तत्तत्प्राप्य शुभाशुभम्।
नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता

transliteration.text:
yaḥ sarvatrānabhisnehastattatprāpya śubhāśubham|
nābhinandati na dveṣṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: When, again, as a tortoise draws in on all sides its limbs, he withdraws his senses from the objects of sense, then is his understanding well poised.

original.text:

इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता

indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyastasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: The objects of sense, but not the relish for them, turn away from an abstemious dweller in the body; and even relish turneth away from him after the Supreme is seen.

original.text:

रसवर्जं रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्तते

transliteration.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: O son of Kuntî, the excited senses of even a wise man, though he be striving, impetuously carry away his mind.

original.text:

इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः

transliteration.text:

indriyāṇi pramāthīni haranti prasabhaṃ manaḥ
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Having restrained them all, he should sit harmonised, I his supreme goal; for, whose senses are mastered, of him the understanding is well poised.

original.text:

transliteration.text:

vaśe hi yasyendriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Man, musing on the objects of sense, conceiveth an attachment to these; from attachment ariseth desire; from desire anger cometh forth;

original.text:

सङ्गात् संजायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: From anger proceedeth delusion; from delusion confused memory; from confused memory the destruction of Reason; from destruction of Reason he perishes.

original.text:
क्रोधाद्भवति संमोहः संमोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः।
स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति

transliteration.text:

smṛtibhraṃśād buddhināśo buddhināśātpraṇaśyati
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: But the disciplined self, moving among sense-objects with senses free from attraction and repulsion, mastered by the Self, goeth to peace.

original.text:

आत्मवश्यैर्विधेयात्मा प्रसादमधिगच्छति

transliteration.text:

ātmavaśyairvidheyātmā prasādamadhigacchati
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: In that Peace the extinction of all pains ariseth for him, for of him whose heart is peaceful the Reason soon attaineth equilibrium.

original.text:

प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्याशु बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते

transliteration.text:

prasannacetaso hyāśu buddhiḥ paryavatiṣṭhate
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: There is no Pure Reason for the non-harmonised, nor for the non-harmonised is there concentration; for him without concentration there is no peace, and for the unpeaceful how can there be happiness?

original.text:
नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना।
न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम्

transliteration.text:

na cābhāvayataḥ śāntiraśāntasya kutaḥ sukham
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Such of the roving senses as the mind yieldeth to, that hurries away the understanding, just as the gale hurries away a ship upon the waters.

original.text:

transliteration.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Therefore, O mighty-armed, whose senses are all completely restrained from the objects of sense, of him the understanding is well poised.

original.text:
तस्माद्यस्य महाबाहो निगृहीतानि सर्वशः।
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता

transliteration.text:

indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyastasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: That which is the night of all beings, for the disciplined man is the time of waking; when other beings are waking, then is it night for the sage who seeth.

original.text:
या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी।
यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः

transliteration.text:

yasyāṃ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśā paśyato muneḥ
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: He attaineth Peace, into whom all desires flow as rivers flow into the ocean, which is filled with water, but remaineth unmoved—not he who desireth desires.

original.text:
आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं
समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत्।
तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे
स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी

transliteration.text:

sa śāntimāpnoti na kāmakāmī
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Whoso forsaketh all desires and goeth onwards free from yearnings, selfless and without egoism—he goeth to Peace.

original.text:

निर्ममो निरहंकारः स शांतिमधिगच्छति

transliteration.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: This is the Eternal state, O son of Prithâ. Having attained thereto, none is bewildered. Who, even at the death-hour, is established therein, he goeth to the Nirvâna of the Eternal.

original.text:
एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति।
स्थित्वाऽस्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृच्छति

transliteration.text:
eṣā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṃ prāpya vimuhyati|
sthitvā'syāmantakāle'pi brahmanirvāṇamṛcchati
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Arjuna said: If it be thought by Thee that knowledge is superior to action, O Janârdana, why dost Thou, O Keshava, enjoin on me this terrible action?

original.text:

तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव

transliteration.text:
arjuna uvāca
jyāyasī cetkarmaṇaste matā buddhirjanārdana|
tatkiṃ karmaṇi ghore māṃ niyojayasi keśava
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: With these perplexing words Thou only confusest my understanding; therefore tell me with certainty the one way by which I may reach bliss.

original.text:

तदेकं वद निश्िचत्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम्

transliteration.text:
vyāmiśreṇeva vākyena buddhiṃ mohayasīva me|
tadekaṃ vada niśicatya yena śreyo'hamāpnuyām
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: The Blessed Lord said: In this world there is a twofold path, as I before said, O sinless one: that of yoga by knowledge, of the Sâñkhyas; and that of yoga by action, of the Yogis.

original.text:
श्री भगवानुवाच

ज्ञानयोगेन सांख्यानां कर्मयोगेन योगिनाम्

transliteration.text:
śrī bhagavānuvāca
loke'smindvividhā niṣṭhā purā proktā mayānagha|

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Man winneth not freedom from action by abstaining from activity, nor by mere renunciation doth he rise to perfection.

original.text:

transliteration.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Nor can anyone, even for an instant, remain really actionless; for helplessly is everyone driven to action by the qualities born of nature.

original.text:

transliteration.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Who sitteth, controlling the organs of action, but dwelling in his mind on the objects of the senses, that bewildered man is called a hypocrite.

original.text:

इन्द्रियार्थान्विमूढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते

transliteration.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: But who, controlling the senses by the mind, O Arjuna, with the organs of action without attachment, performeth yoga by action, he is worthy.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Perform thou right action, for, action is superior to inaction, and, inactive, even the maintenance of thy body would not be possible.

original.text:

शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः

transliteration.text:

śarīrayātrāpi ca te na prasiddhyedakarmaṇaḥ
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: The world is bound by action, unless performed for the sake of sacrifice; for that sake, free from attachment, O son of Kuntî, perform thou action.

original.text:

transliteration.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Having in ancient times emanated mankind together with sacrifice, the Lord of emanation said: "By this shall ye propagate; be this to you the giver of desire;

original.text:

अनेन प्रसविष्यध्वमेष वोऽस्त्विष्टकामधुक्

transliteration.text:

anena prasaviṣyadhvameṣa vo'stviṣṭakāmadhuk
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: "With this nourish ye the Shining Ones, and may the Shining Ones nourish you; thus nourishing one another ye shall reap the supremest good.

original.text:

परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ

transliteration.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: "For, nourished by sacrifice, the Shining Ones shall bestow on you the enjoyments you desire." A thief verily is he who enjoyeth what is given by Them without returning Them aught.

original.text:
इष्टान्भोगान्हि वो देवा दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः।
तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः

transliteration.text:
iṣṭānbhogānhi vo devā dāsyante yajñabhāvitāḥ|

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: The righteous, who eat the remains of the sacrifice, are freed from all sins; but the impious, who dress food for their own sakes, they verily eat sin.

original.text:
यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः।
भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात्

transliteration.text:

bhuñjate te tvaghaṃ pāpā ye pacantyātmakāraṇāt
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: From food creatures become; from rain is the production of food; rain proceedeth from sacrifice; sacrifice ariseth out of action.

original.text:
अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः।
यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः

transliteration.text:
annādbhavanti bhūtāni parjanyādannasambhavaḥ|

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Know thou that from Brahma action groweth, and Brahma from the Imperishable cometh. Therefore the Eternal, the all-permeating, is ever present in sacrifice.

original.text:
कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम्।
तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम्

transliteration.text:
karma brahmodbhavaṃ viddhi brahmākṣarasamudbhavam|
tasmātsarvagataṃ brahma nityaṃ yajñe pratiṣṭhitam
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: He who on earth doth not follow the wheel thus revolving, sinful of life and rejoicing in the senses, he, O son of Pritha, liveth in vain.

original.text:
एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः।
अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति

transliteration.text:
evaṃ pravartitaṃ cakraṃ nānuvartayatīha yaḥ|
aghāyurindriyārāmo moghaṃ pārtha sa jīvati
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: But the man who rejoiceth in the Self, with the Self is satisfied, and is content in the Self, for him verily there is nothing to do;

original.text:
यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः।
आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते

transliteration.text:
yastvātmaratireva syādātmatṛptaśca mānavaḥ|
ātmanyeva ca santuṣṭastasya kāryaṃ na vidyate
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: For him there is no interest in things done, in this world, nor any in things not done, nor doth any object of his depend on any being.

original.text:
नैव तस्य कृतेनार्थो नाकृतेनेह कश्चन।
न चास्य सर्वभूतेषु कश्िचदर्थव्यपाश्रयः

transliteration.text:
naiva tasya kṛtenārtho nākṛteneha kaścana|
na cāsya sarvabhūteṣu kaśicadarthavyapāśrayaḥ
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Therefore, without attachment, constantly perform action which is duty, for, by performing action without attachment, man verily reacheth the Supreme.

original.text:
तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर।
असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः

transliteration.text:
tasmādasaktaḥ satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara|
asakto hyācarankarma paramāpnoti pūruṣaḥ
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Janaka and others indeed attained to perfection by action: then having an eye to the welfare of he world also, thou shouldst perform action.

original.text:
कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः।
लोकसंग्रहमेवापि संपश्यन्कर्तुमर्हसि

transliteration.text:
karmaṇaiva hi saṃsiddhimāsthitā janakādayaḥ|
lokasaṃgrahamevāpi saṃpaśyankartumarhasi
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Whatsoever a great man doeth, that other men also do; the standard he setteth up, by that the people go.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: There is nothing in the three worlds, O Pârtha, that should be done by Me, nor anything unattained that might be attained; yet I mingle in action.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: For if I mingled not ever in action unwearied, men all around would follow My path, O son of Prithâ.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: These worlds would fall into ruin, if I did not perform action; I should be the author of confusion of castes, and should destroy these creatures.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: As the ignorant act from attachment to action, O Bhârata, so should the wise act without attachment, desiring the welfare of the world.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Let no wise man unsettle the mind of ignorant people attached to action; but acting in harmony with Me let him render all action attractive.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: All actions are wrought by the quali ties of nature only. The self, deluded by egoism, thinketh: "I am the doer."

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: But he, O mighty-armed, who knoweth the essence of the divisions of the qualities and functions, holding that "the qualities move amid the qualities," is not attached.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Those deluded by the qualities of nature are attached to the functions of the qualities. The man of perfect knowledge should not unsettle the foolish whose knowledge is imperfect.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Surrendering all actions to Me, with thy thoughts resting on the supreme Self, from hope and egoism freed, and of mental fever cured, engage in battle.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Who abide ever in this teaching of Mine full of faith and free from caviling, they too are released from actions.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Who carp at My teaching and act not thereon, senseless, deluded in all knowledge, know thou these mindless ones as fated to be destroyed.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Even the man of knowledge behaves in conformity with his own nature; beings follow nature; what shall restraint avail?

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Affection and aversion for the objects of sense abide in the senses; let none come under the dominion of these two; they are obstructors of the path.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Better one's own duty, though destitute of merit, than the duty of another, well discharged. Better death in the discharge of one's own duty; the duty of another is full of danger.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Arjuna said: But dragged on by what does a man commit sin, reluctantly indeed, O Varshneya, as it were by force constrained?

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: The Blessed Lord said: It is desire, it is wrath, begotten by the quality of motion; all-consuming, all-polluting, know thou this as our foe here on earth.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: As a flame is enveloped by smoke, as a mirror by dust, as an embryo is wrapped by the amnion, so This is enveloped by it.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Enveloped is wisdom by this constant enemy of the wise in the form of desire, which is insatiable as a flame.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: The senses, the mind and the Reason are said to be its seat; by these enveloping wisdom, it bewilders the dweller in the body.

translation.text: Therefore, O best of the Bhâratas, mastering first the senses, do thou slay this thing of sin, destructive of wisdom and knowledge.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: It is said that the senses are great; greater than the senses is the mind: greater than the mind is the Reason; but what is greater than the Reason, is He.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Thus understanding Him as greater than the Reason, restraining the self by the Self, slay thou, O mighty-armed, the enemy in the form of desire, difficult to overcome.

translation.text: The Blessed Lord said: This imperishable yoga I declared to Vivasvân; Vivasvân taught it to Manu; Manu to Ikshvâku told it.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: This, handed on down the line, the King-Sages knew. This yoga by great efflux of time decayed in the world, O Parantapa.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: This same ancient yoga hath been to-day declared to thee by Me, for thou art My devotee and My friend; it is the supreme Secret.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Arjuna said: Later was Thy birth, earlier the birth of Vivasvân; how then am I to understand that Thou declaredst it in the beginning?

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: The Blessed Lord said: Many births have been left behind by Me and by thee, O Arjuna. I know them all, but thou knowest not thine, O Parantapa.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Though unborn, the imperishable Self, and also the Lord of all beings, brooding over nature which is Mine own, yet I am born through My own Power.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Whenever there is decay of righteousness, O Bhârata, and there is exaltation of unrighteousness, then I Myself come forth;

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: For the protection of the good, for the destruction of evil-doers, for the sake of firmly establishing righteousness, I am born from age to age.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: He who thus knoweth My divine birth and action, in its essence, having abandoned the body, cometh not to birth again, but cometh unto Me, O Arjuna.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Freed from passion, fear and anger, filled with Me, taking refuge in Me, purified in the fire of wisdom, many have entered into My Being.

original.text:

बहवो ज्ञानतपसा पूता मद्भावमागताः

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: However men approach Me, even so do I welcome them, for the path men take from every side is Mine, O Pârtha.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: They who long after success in action on earth worship the Shining Ones; for in brief space verily, in this world of men, success is born of action.

original.text:

क्षिप्रं हि मानुषे लोके सिद्धिर्भवति कर्मजा

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: The four castes were emanated by Me, by the different distribution of qualities and actions; know Me to be the author of them, though the actionless and inexhaustible.

तस्य कर्तारमपि मां विद्ध्यकर्तारमव्ययम्

translation.text: Nor do actions affect Me, nor is the fruit of action desired by Me. He who thus knoweth Me is not bound by actions.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Having thus known, our forefathers, ever seeking liberation, performed action; therefore do thou also perform action, as did our forefathers in the olden time.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: "What is action, what inaction"? Even the wise are herein perplexed. Therefore I will declare to thee the action by knowing which thou shalt be loosed from evil.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: It is needful to discriminate action, to discriminate unlawful action, and to discriminate inaction; mysterious is the path of action.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: He who seeth inaction in action, and action in inaction, he is wise among men, he is harmonious, even while performing all action.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Whose works are all free from the moulding of desire, whose actions are burned up by the fire of wisdom, him the wise have called a Sage.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Having abandoned attachment to the fruit of action, always content, nowhere seeking refuge, he is not doing anything, although doing actions.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Hoping for naught, his mind and self controlled, having abandoned all greed, performing action by the body alone, he doth not commit sin.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Content with whatsoever he obtaineth without effort, free from the pairs of opposites, without envy, balanced in success and failure, though acting he is not bound.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Of one with attachment dead, harmonious, with his thoughts established in wisdom, his works sacrifices, all action melts away.

original.text:

transliteration.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: The Eternal the oblation, the Eternal the clarified butter, are offered in the Eternal the fire by the Eternal; unto the Eternal verily shall he go who in his action meditateth wholly upon the Eternal.

original.text:
ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्महविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम्।
ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना

transliteration.text:

brahmaiva tena gantavyaṃ brahmakarmasamādhinā
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Some Yogis offer up sacrifice to the Shining Ones; others sacrifice only by pouring sacrifice into the fire of the Eternal;

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Some pour as sacrifice hearing and the other senses into the fires of restraint; some pour sound and the other objects of sense into the fires of the senses as sacrifice;

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Others again into the wisdom-kindled fire of union attained by self-control, pour as sacrifice all the functions of the senses and the functions of life;

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Yet others the sacrifice of wealth, the sacrifice of austerity, the sacrifice of yoga, the sacrifice of silent reading and wisdom, men concentrated and of effectual vows;

original.text:
द्रव्ययज्ञास्तपोयज्ञा योगयज्ञास्तथापरे।
स्वाध्यायज्ञानयज्ञाश्च यतयः संशितव्रताः

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Yet others pour as sacrifice the outgoing breath in the incoming, and the incoming in the outgoing, restraining the flow of the outgoing and incoming breaths, solely absorbed in the control of breathing.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Others regular in food, pour as sacrifice their life-breaths in life-breaths. All these are knowers of sacrifice, and by sacrifice have destroyed their sins.

original.text:

translation.text: The eaters of the life-giving remains of sacrifice go to the changeless Eternal. This world is not for the non-sacrificer, much less the other, O best of the Kurus.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Many and various sacrifices are thus spread out before the Eternal. Know thou that all these are born of action, and thus knowing thou shalt be free.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Better than the sacrifice of any objects is the sacrifice of wisdom, O Parantapa. All actions in their entirety, O Pârtha, culminate in wisdom.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Learn thou this by discipleship, by investiga tion, and by service. The wise, the seers of the essence of things, will instruct thee in wisdom.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: And having known this, thou shalt not again fall into this confusion, O Pândava; for by this thou wilt see all beings without exception in the Self, and thus in Me.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Even if thou art the most sinful of all sinners, yet shalt thou cross over all sin by the raft of wisdom.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: As the burning fire reduces fuel to ashes, O Arjuna, so doth the fire of wisdom reduce all actions to ashes.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Verily there is no purifier in this world like wisdom; he that is perfected in yoga finds it in the Self in due season.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: The man who is full of faith obtaineth wisdom, and he also who hath mastery over his senses; and, having obtained wisdom, he goeth swiftly to the supreme Peace.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: But the ignorant, faithless, doubting self goeth to destruction; nor this world, nor that beyond, nor happiness, is there for the doubting self.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: He who hath renounced actions by yoga, who hath cloven asunder doubt by wisdom, who is ruled by the Self, actions do not bind him, O Dhananjaya.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Therefore, with the sword of the wisdom of the Self cleaving asunder this ignorance-born doubt dwelling in thy heart, be established in yoga. Stand up, O Bhârata.

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: Arjuna said: Renunciation of actions Thou praisest, O Krishna, and then also yoga. Of the two which one is the better? That tell me conclusively.

original.text:
अर्जुन उवाच
संन्यासं कर्मणां कृष्ण पुनर्योगं च शंससि।
यच्छ्रेय एतयोरेकं तन्मे ब्रूहि सुनिश्िचतम्

transliteration.text:
arjuna uvāca
saṃnyāsaṃ karmaṇāṃ kṛṣṇa punaryogaṃ ca śaṃsasi|

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

speaker: Arjuna

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: The Blessed Lord said: Renunciation and yoga by action both lead to the highest bliss; of the two, yoga by action is verily better than renunciation of action.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

speaker: The Blessed Lord

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: He should be known as a perpetual ascetic, who neither hateth nor desireth; free from the pairs of opposites, O mighty-armed, he is easily set free from bondage.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: Children, not sages, speak of the Sânkhya and the Yoga as different; he who is duly established in one obtaineth the fruits of both.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: That place which is gained by the Sânkhyas is reached by the Yogîs also. He seeth, who seeth that the Sânkhya and the Yoga are one.

original.text:

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: But without yoga, O mighty-armed, renunciation is hard to attain to; the yoga-harmonised Muni swiftly goeth to the Eternal.

original.text:

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: "I do not anything," should think the harmonised one, who knoweth the essence of things; seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, moving, sleeping, breathing.

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: Speaking, giving, grasping, opening and closing the eyes, he holdeth: "The senses move among the objects of the senses."

original.text:

इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेषु वर्तन्त इति धारयन्

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: He who acteth, placing all actions in the Eternal, abandoning attachment, is unaffected by sin as a lotus leaf by the waters.

original.text:

लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा

transliteration.text:
brahmaṇyādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ|

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: Yogis, having abandoned attachment, perform action only by the body, by the mind, by the Reason, and even by the senses, for the purification of the self.

original.text:
कायेन मनसा बुद्ध्या केवलैरिन्द्रियैरपि।
योगिनः कर्म कुर्वन्ति सङ्गं त्यक्त्वाऽऽत्मशुद्धये

transliteration.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: The harmonised man, having abandoned the fruit of action, attaineth to the eternal Peace; the non-harmonised, impelled by desire, attached to fruit, are bound.

original.text:
युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम्।

transliteration.text:

ayuktaḥ kāmakāreṇa phale sakto nibadhyate
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: Mentally renouncing all actions, the sovereign dweller in the body resteth serenely in the nine-gated city, neither acting nor causing to act.

original.text:
सर्वकर्माणि मनसा संन्यस्यास्ते सुखं वशी।
नवद्वारे पुरे देही नैव कुर्वन्न कारयन्

transliteration.text:
sarvakarmāṇi manasā saṃnyasyāste sukhaṃ vaśī|
navadvāre pure dehī naiva kurvanna kārayan
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: The Lord of the world produceth not the idea of agency, nor actions, nor the union together of action and its fruit; nature, however, manifesteth.

original.text:

न कर्मफलसंयोगं स्वभावस्तु प्रवर्तते

transliteration.text:

na karmaphalasaṃyogaṃ svabhāvastu pravartate
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: The Lord accepteth neither the evil-doing nor yet the well-doing of any. Wisdom is enveloped by unwisdom; therewith mortals are deluded.

original.text:

अज्ञानेनावृतं ज्ञानं तेन मुह्यन्ति जन्तवः

transliteration.text:

ajñānenāvṛtaṃ jñānaṃ tena muhyanti jantavaḥ
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: Verily, in whom unwisdom is destroyed by the wisdom of the Self, in them wisdom, shining as the sun, reveals the Supreme.

original.text:

तेषामादित्यवज्ज्ञानं प्रकाशयति तत्परम्

transliteration.text:

teṣāmādityavajjñānaṃ prakāśayati tatparam
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: Thinking on That, merged in That, established in That, solely devoted to That, they go whence there is no return, their sins dispelled by wisdom.

original.text:

गच्छन्त्यपुनरावृत्तिं ज्ञाननिर्धूतकल्मषाः

transliteration.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: Sages look equally on a Brâhmana adorned with learning and humility, a cow, an elephant, and even a dog and an outcaste.

original.text:
विद्याविनयसंपन्ने ब्राह्मणे गवि हस्तिनि।
शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः

transliteration.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: Even here on earth everything is overcome by those whose mind remains balanced; the Eternal is incorruptible and balanced; therefore they are established in the Eternal.

original.text:

transliteration.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: With Reason firm, unperplexed, the knower of the Eternal established in the Eternal, neither rejoiceth on obtaining what is pleasant, nor sorroweth on obtaining what is unpleasant.

original.text:
न प्रहृष्येत्प्रियं प्राप्य नोद्विजेत्प्राप्य चाप्रियम्।

transliteration.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: He, whose self is unattached to external contacts and findeth joy in the Self, having the self harmonised with the Eternal by yoga, enjoys imperishable bliss.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: The delights that are contact-born, they are verily wombs of pain, for they have beginning and ending, O Kaunteya; not in them may rejoice the wise.

original.text:

आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: He who is able to endure here on earth, ere he be liberated from the body, the force born from desire and passion, he is harmonised, he is a happy man.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: He who is happy within, who rejoiceth within, who is illuminated within, that Yogî, becoming the Eternal, goeth to the Peace of the Eternal.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: Rishis, their sins destroyed, their duality removed, their selves controlled, intent upon the welfare of all beings, obtain the Peace of the Eternal.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: The Peace of the Eternal lies near to those who know themselves, who are disjoined from desire and passion, subdued in nature, of subdued thoughts.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: Having external contacts excluded, and with gaze fixed between the eyebrows; having made equal the outgoing and ingoing breaths moving within the nostrils;

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: With senses, mind, and Reason ever controlled, solely pursuing liberation, the Sage, having for ever cast away desire, fear and passion, verily is liberated.

original.text:

transliteration.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

section: Chapter 5: The Yoga Of The Renunciation Of Action

translation.text: Having known Me, as the Enjoyer of sacrifice and of austerity, the mighty Ruler of all the worlds, and the Lover of all beings, he goeth to Peace.

original.text:
भोक्तारं यज्ञतपसां सर्वलोकमहेश्वरम्।
सुहृदं सर्वभूतानां ज्ञात्वा मां शान्तिमृच्छति

transliteration.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: The Blessed Lord said: He that performeth such action as his duty, independently of the fruit of action, he is an ascetic, he is a Yogî, not he that is without fire, and without rites.

अनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः।

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: That which is called renunciation, know thou that as yoga, O Pândava; nor doth any one become a Yogî with the formative will unrenounced.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: For a Sage who is seeking Yoga, action is called the means; for the same Sage, when he is enthroned in yoga, serenity is called the means.

original.text:
आरुरुक्षोर्मुनेर्योगं कर्म कारणमुच्यते।
योगारूढस्य तस्यैव शमः कारणमुच्यते

transliteration.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: When a man feeleth no attachment either for the objects of sense or for actions, renouncing the formative will, then, he is said to be enthroned in yoga.

original.text:

सर्वसङ्कल्पसंन्यासी योगारूढस्तदोच्यते

transliteration.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Let him raise the self by the Self and not let the self become depressed; for verily is the Self the friend of the self, and also the Self the self's enemy;

original.text:
उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत्।
आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः

transliteration.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: The Self is the friend of the self of him in whom the self by the Self is vanquished; but to the unsubdued self the Self verily becometh hostile as an enemy.

original.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: The higher Self of him who is Self -controlled and peaceful is uniform in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, as well as in honour and dishonour.

original.text:
जितात्मनः प्रशान्तस्य परमात्मा समाहितः।

transliteration.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: The Yogî who is satisfied with wisdom and knowledge, unwavering, whose senses are sub dued, to whom a lump of earth, a stone and gold are the same, is said to be harmonised.

original.text:
ज्ञानविज्ञानतृप्तात्मा कूटस्थो विजितेन्द्रियः।
युक्त इत्युच्यते योगी समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः

transliteration.text:

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: He who regards impartially lovers, friends, and foes, strangers, neutrals, foreigners and relatives, also the righteous and unrighteous, he excelleth.

original.text:

साधुष्वपि च पापेषु समबुद्धिर्विशिष्यते

transliteration.text:

sādhuṣvapi ca pāpeṣu samabuddhirviśiṣyate
transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Let the Yogî constantly engage himself in yoga, remaining in a secret place by himself, with thought and self subdued, free from hope and greed.

original.text:
योगी युञ्जीत सततमात्मानं रहसि स्थितः।
एकाकी यतचित्तात्मा निराशीरपरिग्रहः

transliteration.text:
yogī yuñjīta satatamātmānaṃ rahasi sthitaḥ|

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: When his subdued thought is fixed on the Self, free from longing after all desirable things, then it is said, "he is harmonised."

translation.text: As a lamp in a windless place flickereth not, to such is likened the Yogî of subdued thought, absorbed in the yoga of the Self.

translation.text: That in which the mind finds rest, quieted by the practice of yoga: that in which he, seeing the Self by the Self, in the Self is satisfied;

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: That in which he findeth the supreme delight which the Reason can grasp beyond the senses, wherein established he moveth not from the Reality;

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Which, having obtained, he thinketh there is no greater gain beyond it; wherein, established, he is not shaken even by heavy sorrow;

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: That should be known by the name of yoga, this disconnection from the union with pain. This yoga must be clung to with a firm conviction and with undesponding mind.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Abandoning without reserve all desires born of the imagination, by the mind curbing in the aggregate of the senses on every side,

translation.text: Little by little let him gain tranquillity, by means of Reason controlled by steadiness; having made the mind abide in the Self, let him not think of anything.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: Supreme joy is for this Yogi whose mind is peaceful, whose passion-nature is calmed, who is sinless and of the nature of the Eternal.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: The Yogî who thus, ever harmonising the self, hath put away sin, he easily enjoyeth the infinite bliss of contact with the Eternal.

transliteration.method: Generated from the Devanagari with indic-transliteration (MIT)

translation.text: The self, harmonised by yoga, seeth the Self abiding in all beings, all beings in the Self; everywhere he seeth the same.

translation.text: He who, through the likeness of the Self, O Arjuna, seeth equality in everything, whether pleasant or painful, he is considered a perfect Yogî.

translation.text: For the mind is verily restless, O Krishna; it is impetuous, strong and difficult to bend. I deem it as hard to curb as the wind.

translation.text: The Blessed Lord said: Without doubt, O mighty-armed, the mind is hard to curb and restless; but it may be curbed by constant practice and by dispassion.

translation.text: Yoga is hard to attain, methinks, by a self that is uncontrolled; but by the Self -controlled it is attainable by properly directed energy.

translation.text: Arjuna said: He who is unsubdued but who possesseth faith, with the mind wandering away from yoga, failing to attain perfection in yoga, what path doth he tread, O Krishna?

translation.text: Deign, O Krishna, to completely dispel this doubt of mine; for there is none to be found save Thyself able to destroy this doubt.

translation.text: The Blessed Lord said: O son of Prithâ, neither in this world nor in the life to come is there destruction for him; never doth any who worketh righteousness, O beloved, tread the path of woe.

translation.text: Having attained to the worlds of the pure-doing, and having dwelt there for immemorial years, he who fell from yoga is reborn in a pure and blessed house;

translation.text: Or he may even be born into a family of wise Yogîs; but such a birth as that is most difficult to obtain in this world.

translation.text: There he recovereth the characteristics belonging to this former body, and with these he again laboureth for perfection, O joy of the Kurus.

translation.text: By that former practice he is irresistibly swept away. Only wishing to know yoga, even the seeker after yoga goeth beyond the Brâhmic world;

translation.text: But the Yogî, labouring with assiduity, purified from sin, fully perfected through manifold births, he reacheth the supreme goal.

translation.text: The Yogî is greater than the ascetics; he is thought to be greater than even the wise; the Yogî is greater than the men of action; therefore become thou a Yogî, O Arjuna!

transliteration.text:
